name: Saddam Hussein
role: President of Iraq (1979-2003) and leader of the Ba'ath Party
summary: Saddam Hussein ruled Iraq as a single-party Ba'athist state combining Arab nationalism, state-planned socialism with a limited private sector, and personal authoritarian rule. He nationalised oil, promoted women's education and work, fought wars with Iran and Kuwait, and suppressed Kurdish, Shia and party opponents; from 1991-93 his regime moved from secular Ba'athism to a state religious campaign.

sources.title: FBI interviews and conversations with Saddam Hussein in custody, 2004 (declassified FBI summaries, National Security Archive release)
sources.author: Federal Bureau of Investigation (SSA George Piro and others)
sources.usedFor: His 2004 statements on religion and government, Israel and Palestine, Arab unity, Kuwait, Iran, the UN, his rule and elections.

sources.usedFor: His speeches on oil nationalisation, Kurdish autonomy, the Ba'ath leading party, the army and the Front.

sources.author: Saddam Hussein

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: His party's report he led says people working by their own will for private employers are not exploited, with wages, hours and leave fixed by law, and his 1987 speech keeps workers on wages as state employees.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Told the FBI that Israel's control of Arab lands is the root of the region's problems and that Kuwaitis 'were asking' Iraq to invade; he did not address annexation without consent as such, so the evidence points both ways.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Asked whether Iraq aided Arabs, Kurds and Bakhtiar followers in Iran he said opposition members who came to Iraq received a 'double greeting'.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: His Ba'th party seized power by coup in 1968 (Library of Congress study), but he did not state a general theory of armed vanguard groups.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The constitution prohibits any activity against the objectives of the people and he banned the Dawa Party and expelled the Communists from the Front for violating its principles.

central-planning.rationale: Governed through national development plans with the state holding the central economic links while allowing a private sector; his stated model was planned socialism with private activity alongside.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Told the FBI he ordered missile strikes on Iran's capital in the 'war of the cities' in response to Iranian strikes on Baghdad, and gave the order to fire Scuds at Israel to hurt it.

civilizational-union.rationale: Constitution and speeches state the basic objective of realising one Arab state; told the FBI the Arab nation is one nation with the same language, borders and aims.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said the party has neither encouraged class struggle nor made it an ideological platform, and that the workers' condition changes only with the whole people's through one comprehensive revolution.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Said the party neither encouraged class struggle nor made it an ideological platform and that changing the workers' situation cannot be done without changing the whole people's.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports he ordered the 1980 executions of Baqir as-Sadr, the Dawa leader whose programme resembled Khomeini's, and fought the war with Khomeini's Iran.

collective-defense.rationale: Backed the National Declaration under which Arab states fight together against any foreigner who attacks Arab land or interests.

collective-farming.rationale: Supported enlarging individual farmers' allotments of land in 1980 as long as this did not create social or political influence contrary to socialism, rather than collectivising farms.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Nulled (2026-11-12 pass): the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia; none of the sources opened this pass records his position on colonial-era treaties.

conscription.rationale: The constitution under his rule makes conscription compulsory and calls defence of the homeland a sacred duty.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Spoke of popular legitimacy while holding uncontested referendums with reported 99-100% approval and ruling through terror; the record wins.

death-penalty.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports RCC Law 32 of 1982 and Resolution 1370 making desertion, conspiracy against the state and other offences punishable by death; Human Rights Watch documents mass executions of detainees.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Described a system in which every Iraqi has a permanent source of living, including those who cannot work who receive a wage equal to an unskilled labourer's, and expanded social security in the constitution.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Described Iraqi democracy as 'people's democracy' expressed by consultation, newspaper discussion and an assembly of Ba'athist-led membership, not by competitive elections.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nulled (2026-11-12 pass): the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia; none of the sources opened this pass records his position on the statement.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Told the FBI that after the 1995 and 2002 votes 'the people did, in fact, vote for and elect' him and he owed them obligation, but the votes were single-candidate referendums and he took power through the RCC.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Demanded equality of rights and rejected second-class status, yet said women are less suited to permanent combat service and better suited than men to childcare, and favoured balance rather than identical treatment.

dominated-front.rationale: Urged solidarity among Third World and non-aligned countries to protect independence from superpowers, while keeping friendship with the USSR.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The constitution under his rule makes social solidarity the first foundation, with each citizen accomplishing duty in full and the state guaranteeing rights; defence of the homeland is a sacred duty.

elective-rulers.rationale: Told the FBI that after the 1995 and 2002 votes 'the people did, in fact, vote for and elect' him, but he held the presidency from 1979 as RCC chairman.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports the 1979 trials and executions of high-ranking Baathists and his ordering of the executions of Baqir as-Sadr and his sister in 1980.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the FBI the UN had exceeded its authority and charter regarding Iraq and that sanctions followed US positions; he rejected UN inspections for years.

equal-conscription.rationale: Said women's inability to serve on a large scale and permanently in combat units does not undermine equality and that men are better suited to the army; conscription applied to men.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution under his rule declares citizens equal before the law regardless of sex, origin, language or religion, while Human Rights Watch documents the persecution of Kurds, Shia and opponents.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said no one can object to income differences based on academic achievement, work hazards, skill and performance, objecting only to differences inherited from pre-revolution conditions.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Defended Iraq's nuclear technology programme with France and Italy as aimed at peaceful uses and said the atom is widely used for peaceful purposes.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Human Rights Watch documents the repression of the 1991 Kurdish and Shia uprisings and the 1988 Anfal campaign against Kurdish areas; the Library of Congress study covers the war on Barzani's Kurdish rebellion.

force-without-un.rationale: Invaded Iran in 1980 (Library of Congress study) and occupied Kuwait in 1990, which drew UN sanctions that stayed for years (Human Rights Watch).

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The constitution of his government prohibits immobile (real estate) ownership by non-Iraqis except where a law allows.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Told the FBI that Iran intended to annex southern Iraq and that the US and 'Zionist' influence conspired against Iraq.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The constitution under his rule commits the state to free education and free medical care, and his party report says all citizens enjoy free services in education, health and other fields.

free-public-college.rationale: The constitution under his rule guarantees free education at primary, secondary and university stages.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports that in 1979 he became president, chairman of the RCC and commander in chief of the armed forces, and that the president is chief executive of the RCC and head of government and state.

independent-unions.rationale: The Library of Congress study records that state workers' unions were government-sponsored and that in 1987 government workers were barred from union membership while private-sector unions were allowed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said each nation has its own particular programme and form of socialism and that Iraq's democracy and laws must suit its developing conditions.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Told the FBI the 1948 formation of a separate Jewish state created the problem and that a Palestinian state is the basis of any solution; the war with Israel was 'still on'. His speeches call Israel the 'Zionist entity'.

job-guarantee.rationale: Said every Iraqi who can work 'has an open chance with the State at all times'; the constitution declares work a right ensured to every able citizen.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Nulled (2026-11-12 pass): the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia; none of the sources opened this pass records his position on colonial-era borders.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Called for Arab unity as the goal of the Ba'ath revolution and said there is one Arab world from the simple person to the thinker.

land-redistribution.rationale: His government's Agrarian Reform Law (which he cited) capped agricultural holdings; the constitution gives the surplus above the legal maximum to the people.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Said the Arab nation, from poor to wealthy, is one nation with the same language, common borders and aims, despite state borders.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Baram reports RCC Decree 59 of 1994 and later decrees introduced Qur'anic amputation penalties and transformed the penal code, and Amnesty records the 1990s judicial amputations; the wider legal system stayed largely civil-law based.

leader-cult.rationale: The 1982 party congress report he led adopted the 'Leader-Necessity' formula, calling his leadership a national necessity and rejecting departure from it as damage to the people, while denying it was a cult of personality.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The constitution under his rule calls work a right and a sacred duty of every able citizen, but sets no legal compulsion.

majority-settlement.rationale: Human Rights Watch documents the Arabization campaign that moved Arabs into Kirkuk and other Kurdish areas and the displacement of Kurds in Anfal.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said the socialist sector holds the central links and sets a prices policy that cannot be violated without punishment, letting only 'remoter elements' move freely; private activity is encouraged but guided by the state.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports his government paid extremely generous lifelong benefits to the families of those killed in the war with Iran, calling them martyrs.

military-superiority.rationale: Built one of the region's largest armies; told the FBI Iraq could not appear weak to regional enemies and said its army should serve the entire Arab nation.

minority-language-support.rationale: The constitution under his rule makes Kurdish an official language in the Kurdish region besides Arabic.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Human Rights Watch records that Baghdad decreed a Kurdish autonomy statute in 1974 but also ran a sweeping Arabization campaign in Kurdish areas and the Anfal attacks.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Library of Congress study records his 1987 incentive plan letting state managers award workers up to 30 percent of productivity gains.

more-religion-public.rationale: Baram reports he launched the 1993 Faith Campaign: Qur'an and Hadith study made a national focus, public drinking banned and night clubs cut, new mosques; he notes scholars dispute whether it was belief or strategy.

multipolar-world.rationale: Told the FBI a world of two superpowers was better than now but argued that strengthening Third World and non-aligned countries would blunt superpower spheres of influence.

nation-first.rationale: Stressed Iraq's sovereignty and dignity over outside demands and ignored the Security Council on Kuwait, while saying he wanted a relationship with the US.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Human Rights Watch records that Baghdad decreed a Kurdish autonomy statute in 1974, alongside the later Arabization of Kurdish areas.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Told the FBI he rejected the legitimacy of what was done to Iraq under UN authority, but he never stated that domestic law outranks international law generally.

national-rebirth.rationale: Described the Arab nation as 'in a state of renaissance' and beginning to rise after being kept backward.

national-resource-control.rationale: Led the 1972-73 nationalisation of the foreign oil companies and described it as the revolution's defining act against imperialism.

national-self-determination.rationale: Human Rights Watch documents his denial of a Kurdish state through Arabization and the Anfal campaign, and the occupation of Kuwait.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Said Ba'ath socialism differs basically from other socialist systems (keeps private property alongside a socialist sector), the constitution lists struggle against capitalistic ideology among education goals, and he said the party neither encouraged class struggle nor made it its platform.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Urged stricter and wider conditions on divorce and said unjustified divorce should be condemned everywhere, as part of improving women's position.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Urged Arab states not to give military bases to any foreign power and called Omani base offers to the Americans unacceptable.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Baram reports the Faith Campaign made Qur'an and Hadith study a national focus in schools, with Qur'an teaching programmes for teachers.

one-party-rule.rationale: Described the Ba'ath as 'the leading party' and its theory as the leading theory of Iraqi society; no other political group was allowed to be active in the army, and the Communists were expelled from the National Front.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: Said that polygamy ought to be condemned in every corner of society and that strengthening the conditions that prohibit it is part of women's liberation.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stated that the armed forces receive their orders from the Party and that no political group other than the Ba'ath Party is permitted to be active inside them, citing the Charter of National Action.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports wartime censorship and that the major daily Ath Thawrah was government-run; it does not show the party itself owning all media.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said obstacles in the way of women are greater than those facing men and condemned feudal, tribal and bourgeois outlooks that treat women as second class.

patriotic-education.rationale: The constitution lists as education's aim a generation 'proud of his people, his homeland and heritage' and he promoted it.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports a People's Army militia of 650,000 alongside a regular army of similar size, supplementing rather than replacing it.

person-over-state.rationale: Described the human being, man or woman, as the basic instrument of the party's struggle and called on citizens to sacrifice for the revolution.

population-transfer.rationale: Human Rights Watch documents the deportation of Feyli Kurds, the Arabization of Kirkuk and other areas and the forced expulsion of ethnic minorities; the Library of Congress study reports thousands of Shias of Iranian origin deported in 1980.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Repeatedly invoked Iraq's six-thousand-year civilization and Arab heritage and wrote national pride in heritage into education aims.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rejected the Marxist view that surplus value means exploitation: 'We may have surplus value without exploitation'; an Iraqi working for the private sector 'is not exploited'.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said private property is to be tolerated only within limits set by the socialist programme; the constitution allows expropriation for public interest and bars it where it conflicts with state planning.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Told the press in 1980 that private property continues only 'provided it is socially acceptable', i.e. without a material base giving a minority political or social influence at the people's expense; the constitution calls ownership a social function.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalised the Iraqi oil industry in 1972 and cited it as the core of the revolution; the constitution he presided under states that national resources and basic means of production are owned by the people.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said he believed in God and spoke of obligation to the people 'in front of God'; Ba'athist ideology joined science with faith in the Arab message.

religion-illusion.rationale: His government promoted religion through the 1993 Faith Campaign (Baram), treating it as a lasting social force.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Human Rights Watch documents his government's Arabization campaign that deported Kurds and other minorities from Kirkuk and other areas, and the forced expulsion of ethnic minorities from government-controlled areas.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called at the 1979 Non-Aligned summit for radical changes in the international economic order, an inflation fund for developing countries and producers' associations to confront industrial-country monopolies.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Cited Iraq's goal of regaining the Shatt al-Arab and announced the abrogation of the 1975 Algiers Agreement in 1980.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pursued Arab unity as the goal of the revolution, told the FBI the Arab nation is one nation with the same language and borders, and said Kuwaitis 'were asking' Iraq to invade them.

right-to-secede.rationale: The constitution under his rule states that Iraq's territory is indivisible and no part can be ceded.

separate-church-state.rationale: Baram traces the regime from militant secularism to the 1993 Faith Campaign and Sharia punishments in 1994, so the record points both ways.

separated-powers.rationale: Iraq's constitution made the Revolutionary Command Council, which he chaired, the supreme institution issuing laws with the force of law and electing the president, with immunity for its members.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Called Israel a 'Zionist entity' and the 1948 formation of Israel the 'rape of Palestine' and an aggression against the Arab nation, but did not use the term colonial project.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The constitution under his rule says the state alone establishes the armed forces and no other group may form military or paramilitary formations.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ran five-year development plans (e.g. 1981-85) and Iraq's constitution makes the state responsible for planning, directing and steering the national economy; he said the state holds 'the central links'.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: His government promoted Islamic instruction and religion through the 1993 Faith Campaign (Baram) rather than atheism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said Iraq relies on nobody except Iraq and the Arab nation, belonged to the Non-Aligned Movement and rejected following either superpower.

strong-leader.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports that in practice all party decisions were made by Saddam Husayn and that he viewed the cabinet and the RCC as rubber stamps.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Baram reports the state Ministry of Awqaf produced the 60,000 Qur'an books of the Faith Campaign, which the president launched and directed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports that in 1979 several high-ranking Baathists were tried and executed for allegedly planning a coup and that he dealt ruthlessly with suspected opposition; it adds that between 1968 and 1973 the party eliminated suspected challengers through sham trials, executions and assassinations; Human Rights Watch documents mass arrests and summary executions after the 1991 uprisings.

term-limits.rationale: Held the presidency from 1979 under a constitution with no term limit, and told the FBI the people elected him in 1995 and 2002 and he owed them obligation; accepted no term limit.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Invaded Iran in 1980 (Library of Congress study) and occupied Kuwait in 1990-91 (Human Rights Watch).

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Baram records that RCC decrees under his rule in 1994 prescribed hand and foot amputation, ear cutting and branding as legal punishments, and Amnesty documents systematic torture of political prisoners.

traditional-family.rationale: Called the family 'a living cell' of society and the constitution calls it the nucleus of society to be protected by the state, while rejecting feudal views confining women to the home.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Presented Iraq as 'a civilization of six thousand years' and invoked its ancient heritage in speeches and education aims.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Library of Congress study reports the Ba'th made military training for youth central to creating new men, founding the paramilitary Futuwah youth vanguard for 14-18 year olds in 1975.

unions-good.rationale: Said unions arose to improve workers' conditions and that even slight improvement from union struggle was an achievement to seek, while holding that real change comes through the whole-people revolution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The constitution under his rule commits the state to free medical services in protection, treatment and medicine in cities and rural areas; he said every Iraqi has a guaranteed source of living.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Held the presidency from 1979 under a constitution that has the RCC elect the president with no term limit, and told the FBI the people elected him in 1995 and 2002.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Said private activity should extend in services, production, agriculture and industry within limits, and defended larger farmer allotments, but also kept key sectors in state hands.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said women's radical emancipation cannot be achieved without emancipating the whole society politically, economically and culturally, and that bourgeois concepts of emancipation will not free women.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Said the Agrarian Reform Law made no distinction between men and women; inheritance remained governed by the law as the constitution guarantees it.

women-suffrage.rationale: Declared women one half of society entitled to full participation, and the constitution he presided under makes citizens equal before the law without discrimination because of sex.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said imperialist powers rob the wealth of developing countries, that inflation exported to them costs several times the aid they receive and that the industrialized countries bear the responsibility for most of their damage.

notes: Views changed: the 1970s-80s sources are secular Ba'athist; from 1991 and the 1993 Faith Campaign the regime promoted Islam, but in 2004 he told the FBI religion and government should not mix. Where acts contradict stated principles (equal citizenship, self-determination, democracy), answers are low or 0. Not reached: The Saddam Tapes (Woods, Palkki, Stout), Conflict Records Research Center files, and Social and Foreign Affairs in Iraq (restricted on the Internet Archive); the Al-Khuld Hall tape and Anfal are used only through Wikipedia. Second pass (2026-11-12): the Wikipedia sources of the first pass (s7-s14) are kept only for the history of changed answers; answers now rest on the Library of Congress country study, Baram, Human Rights Watch, Amnesty, his 1982 party congress report and his speeches, and candidate statements are answered. Themes searched in the local library: economy and labour, wages and unions, women and family, religion and the Faith Campaign, ethnic policy (Arabization, deportations), elections and leadership, the Iran and Kuwait wars, the world economy, youth organisations, torture and punishment. No position was found on immigration policy, drug policy, sexuality, technology, ecology, animals, central banking or the other statements left null.
